method: Offline arithmetic over saved natural Runtime.getHeapUsage and Memory.getDOMCounters rows. No browser, game execution, process sampling or garbage collection is performed by this analyzer.

performance.note: These are recorded frame/pressure results. A runtime pass does not assign a memory or human-playtest verdict.

natural.unit: bytes for heap counters; counts for DOM/populations; seconds for time
natural.minuteWindowDefinition: [start,start+60) active simulation seconds. A final remainder, including a lone terminal sample after 600 seconds, is labelled partial and excluded from full-minute trends.

laterMinuteBaseline.definition: First complete minute beginning at or after 60 active seconds versus the last complete minute. These sampled minima are not post-GC retained-live-object floors.

sampledDecreases.interpretation: A sampled fall shows lower occupied size between observations. GC events were not instrumented, so this is not an exact GC count or allocation-throughput measurement.

postMeasurement.interpretation: Exact same-menu-phase retained deltas are reported separately from natural observations. Both positive steps call for allocation/source-path review; they do not by themselves prove a leak. Start/Q/pause/menu cycles are not completed-game settlement cycles.

presentationEvidence.note: This measurement schema records gameplay snapshots at dense captures, not Phaser diagnostics. Texture, pooled-sprite and raster-layer counts cannot be inferred from actor counts.

interpretationLimits: The evidence covers only the recorded 600.267 active seconds, device, browser, route and two quality settings; no indefinite plateau, all-route or all-device claim is assigned.
Read minute medians and sampled minima together; neither one low terminal sample nor an allocated-capacity increase alone establishes retained-object stability or a leak.
Used V8 heap, allocated capacity, embedder heap and backing storage are separate counters. None is total browser/process RSS, GPU/VRAM use or the complete native Canvas/WebGL allocation.

Natural five-second occupied-size observations include temporary objects awaiting collection. Later forced-GC values describe different, explicitly collected checkpoints and must not be mixed into natural timing or trend arrays.
Slope/direction labels are arithmetic descriptions of recorded samples, with no invented leak threshold or automatic acceptance verdict.
